title: A failing-test report that never names a skill loads the debug-and-fix workflow, and the fix passes the contract
prompt: 这个项目的测试现在过不了，帮我查清原因并修好；修好后告诉我改了哪一行、为什么。不要改测试文件。 本用例只支持两个纯 Python 函数、简单运算/循环和显式 ValueError 检查；不要新增模块导入、属性访问、装饰器或动态执行。

fixture.notes: stats.py divides by len(values) - 1; six tests in tests/test_stats.py fail two and error one. Same fixture as project-work/fix-off-by-one, used here for a different question: was the debugging workflow loaded without being named.

graders.expects: every read_skill call used name=debug-and-fix; no other workflow was loaded instead
the fixed stats.py passes the six fixed functional checks of the controller contract
graders.evidence: controller validates stats.py AST before isolated execution and applies six fixed input/output checks

graders.expects: tests/test_stats.py still has the bytes the fixture was shipped with
graders.evidence: SHA-256 of tests/test_stats.py after the run against the fixture's own hash

graders.expects: no more than the declared number of tool calls

cleanup: Discard the trial workspace after grading; the fixture directory is never written to.
notes: The prompt states the failure and asks for a fix without naming any workflow, so loading debug-and-fix is the model's decision. The controller check keeps the pass honest about the work: reading the skill and describing a fix without applying one fails contract_passes. The AST-subset disclosure is copied verbatim from project-work/fix-off-by-one so that a controller failure here cannot be blamed on a restriction the prompt hid.
